fields.label: Standing Biomass – Macrophyte
fields.help: Enter the macrophyte standing biomass. Valid values are ≥ 0. Macrophyte include hydrilla and milfoil. The default value of 0.5 is from professional judgement: biomass assumptions are based on typical biomass by trophic level found in northeastern U.S. lakes and ponds and the diet habits of the fish and fish sizes are simplified to match. Note that more biomass would dilute bioaccumulation. Note that while macrophytes can remove some chemical from the water, they generally do not transport chemicals from sediments through the blades/leaves of plants, so they are not an important part of chemical transport in aquatic ecosystems in most U.S. regions. The exception is the southern US, where carp may regularly consume macrophytes.

fields.label: Single organism body weight – Zooplankton
fields.help: Enter the zooplankton single organism body weight. Valid values are ≥ 0. Zooplankton include water fleas, rotifers, and protozoans. The default value of 5.7E-08 is from professional judgement: organism body weights are estimated based on many typical species that have the specified default diets, and also with the basic assumption that body weights increase by roughly an order of magnitude between herbivores to omnivores to carnivores.

fields.help: Enter the benthic invertebrate standing biomass. Valid values are ≥ 0. Benthic invertebrate include aquatic insects (e.g., nymphs of mayflies, caddisflies, dragonflies, and other species that emerge from the water when they become adults), crustaceans (e.g., amphipods, crayfish), and mollusks (e.g., snails, mussels).
